With a private value of $47, my goal is to maximize potential profit. Since this is a second-price sealed bid auction, I want to bid strategically. A pure optimal strategy is to bid my true value ($47) because:
1. If I win, I'll pay less than my value
2. If I bid less, I risk losing and getting zero profit
3. There's no advantage to bidding below my true value
4. Bidding above my value risks a net loss

My private value is $33. To maximize profit, I want to bid strategically - high enough to have a good chance of winning, but not so high that I lose money if I win. Since values are drawn randomly and independently, I'll aim to bid slightly above the midpoint of the possible range. A bid around $25-$30 gives me a good probability of winning while preserving potential profit margin.

With a private value of $36, I want to maximize potential profit. Since this is a second-price sealed bid auction, my optimal strategy is to bid close to my true value but not exactly at it. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances while protecting downside. A bid around $38-$40 seems strategic - high enough to likely win, but not so high that I risk significant loss if I win. I'll aim to capture most of my value's surplus.
